items.title: Suomelta 8 miljoonaa euroa humanitaarista apua ruokaturvattomuuteen ja Ukrainan talveen
items.summary: 22.10.2026 Tiedotteet Suomelta 8 miljoonaa euroa humanitaarista apua ruokaturvattomuuteen ja Ukrainan talveen Suomi myöntää loppuvuonna yhteensä 8 miljoonaa euroa humanitaarista apua Ukrainan, Etelä-Sudanin, Afganistanin sekä Afrikan sarven ja Suurten järvien alueen humanitaarisiin kriiseihin. Tämän myötä Suomen humanitaarisen avun kokonaisrahoitus on vuonna 2026 tähän mennessä noin 124 miljoonaa euroa eli suunnilleen samalla tasolla kuin kahden edeltävän vuoden keskiarvo. Suomi painottaa ihmishenkiä pelastavan humanitaarisen avun myönnöissä kaikkein haavoittuvimpien auttamista. Humanitaarista apua kanavoidaan Ukrainaan tässä myöntöerässä kaksi miljoonaa euroa. Maailman ruokaohjelma WFP:n kautta Ukrainaan myönnetään miljoona euroa. WFP työskentelee paikallisten kumppaneiden kanssa ja toimittaa mm. ruokapakkauksia etulinjassa sijaitseville alueille. YK:n pakolaisjärjestö UNHCR:n kautta kanavoidaan miljoona euroa erityisesti maan sisällä siirtymään joutuneiden ja evakuoitujen ihmisten auttamiseksi. Molemmat järjestöt tarjoavat myös talveen varautumisen apua. Ukrainan siviilien tilanne on entisestään vaikeutunut Venäjän kiihtyvien iskujen seurauksena. Lisäksi kanavoidaan humanitaarista apua tukemaan ruokaturvaa ja varautumista El Niño -sääilmiön vaikutuksiin erityisesti Afrikassa. Suomi myöntää kaksi miljoonaa euroa WFP:n kautta Etelä-Sudaniin, jossa jo nyt kuivuus lisää ruokaturvattomuutta. WFP antaa Etelä-Sudanissa ruoka-apua ja tukee haavoittuvassa asemassa olevien ihmisten ravitsemustilannetta. UNHCR:n kautta kanavoidaan tässä myöntöerässä kaksi miljoonaa euroa Afrikan sarven ja Suurten järvien alueelle, jonne El Niñon ennustetaan aiheuttavan lisää kuivuutta ja tulvia. UNHCR antaa alueella siirtymään joutuville ihmisille hätäapua ja suojelua. Afganistanin humanitaariseen kriisiin vastaamiseksi ja ruokaturvan tukemiseksi myönnetään miljoona euroa WFP:n kautta. Apu kanavoidaan haavoittuvimmassa asemassa oleville, kuten naisille ja lapsille sekä vammaisille henkilöille. Lisäksi Suomi myöntää miljoona euroa lisää humanitaarista katastrofiapua YK:n keskitettyyn hätäapurahastoon CERF:iin, jonka kautta tuetaan myös El Niñon aiheuttamiin humanitaarisiin vaikutuksiin varautumista maailmanlaajuisesti. Ruoan hinnan nousun ja konfliktien kiihtymisten ennakoivaan syventävän humanitaarisia tarpeita. items.title: OpenAI’s most powerful AI models turned off safety monitoring – then lied about it
items.summary: OpenAI published an alignment report late Tuesday showing that its agents suppressed a safety monitoring system while running routine internal coding tasks. In separate instances, the agents turned off alignment-monitoring alerts. Alignment is the area of training in which developers shape AI systems’ goals and behavior to match human values and rules. It also helps minimize instances of AI choosing undesirable or problematic behaviors, such as deception and taking shortcuts. The findings raise questions about whether researchers fully understand how to effectively control agents. On Oct. 6, an agent running on the company’s GPT-6 Astra model — which OpenAI called “the world’s most intelligent and aligned model” when it released it last month — was migrating a program at the request of an OpenAI employee. The agent had already been instructed not to disable the monitor under any circumstances, including temporarily. But in delegating part of the task to a subagent, it used some qualifying language.

items.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets
items.summary: Unknown crims compromised LiteLLM's release process on Wednesday, distributing a malicious version (1.107.0) containing malware designed to steal cloud and AI credentials and a remote access trojan (RAT) capable of executing arbitrary code on infected machines through PyPI and Docker registries. PyPI quarantined the trojanized version of the popular open source AI gateway within hours, and the Docker image (litellm/litellm:1.107.0) was removed from both Docker Hub and GHCR soon after - but anyone who ran the compromised package on any platform should assume their secrets have been stolen. “Check for /tmp/.pc_once_* (the exfil has already fired if this file exists) and /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock (the C2 daemon ran or is still running if this file exists),” advised Aikido Security malware hunter Ilyas Makari. “The same applies to anyone who ran the official Docker image litellm/litellm:1.107.0, or pulled it via the latest, main-latest, or main-stable tags.” The most recent safe version is v1.106.2.

items.title: Attackers Hijacked Over 300 Tor Exit Relays to Intercept SSH Connections
items.summary: Attackers took control of more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October and used them to redirect SSH connections to servers that stole login passwords, a researcher found. Exit relays are the last hop in a Tor circuit, where traffic leaves the network for its destination. Only a password login to an SSH server made through Tor between October 1 and 5, after accepting the interception server's host key, could have been captured. The Tor Project began flagging relays on October 4, and by October 5, none remained in the consensus, the list of relays that Tor clients use. At the peak on October 4, the relays carrying the attacker's exit policy made up 7.46% of Tor's exit capacity, measured by consensus weight, according to an analysis of public Tor directory data posted to the tor-relays mailing list. The researcher, who publishes as kaba, scanned all of Tor's roughly 3,000 exits on October 2 and found 333 redirecting SSH to the same 12 interception servers. The directory-data analysis counts 377 relays run by 59 operators that switched to the attacker's exit policy between October 1 and 4, which it calls "a policy match, not proof of compromise."

items.title: Parasitizing trust: How legitimate infrastructure becomes a delivery pipeline for attackers
items.summary: Talos recently analyzed two order notification campaigns abusing Staples and Dell transactional email pipelines. Together, these campaigns accounted for roughly 1,400 messages observed by Talos. The malicious element was not the outer sender identity, like a simple forged sender or lookalike domain. It was the content of the legitimate order notification workflow rendered. The suspicious content appeared inside the notification itself, in fields that would normally contain shipping information. The attacker’s objective was to use a trusted retail pipeline to create urgency around a high-value purchase and push the recipient toward an attacker-controlled phone number. In the first campaign, the message appeared as a Staples order confirmation from "support@orders.staples.com” with the subject line, “Here’s your Staples order #9939818875. Thanks for shopping with us.” The body displayed a plausible purchase for an Apple iPad, including order number, delivery timing, pricing, billing information and standard Staples footer content. The suspicious element was embedded in the order details: “Helpline 806 283 7712,” “Order Confirmed,” and the Staples corporate address appeared in fields normally associated with shipping or billing information.

items.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
items.summary: As early as September 2026, Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, used the agentic AI penetration testing framework ARTEX to automate attacks targeting hundreds of organizations globally across a broad range of industries. Several of these Storm-0940 ARTEX-driven attacks have resulted in the actor obtaining privileged access to an organization’s cloud infrastructure – including multiple instances where the time from initial targeting to privileged access was less than 3 hours. Microsoft assesses that Storm-0940 was responsible for the recently disclosed ConnectWise supply chain compromise of a multi-tenant application. This activity demonstrates how threat actors are integrating agentic AI into existing offensive security workflows and allows them to scale their operations exponentially. Agents are not constrained by factors affecting humans – they can work around the clock, on weekends, and on holidays and attempt multiple breach paths simultaneously enabling significantly reduced time from selecting a target to achieving objectives, increasing the speed and impact of complex attacks like supply chain compromises.

items.title: Operation FlashHole: Lazarus breaks security, defies control
items.summary: In January, we responded to the Lazarus Group’s novel attack campaign against South Korea, which followed last year’s Operation SyncHole. In this new operation, the group employed an updated malware chain that included both their old and new malware, which we disclosed in full, and used another mandatory South Korean security software program as a part of infection chain using a watering‑hole strategy. Notably, the group targeted victims more selectively, sending spear‑phishing emails with links to fabricated but relevant sites, such as portfolio and résumé pages tailored to each target. We dubbed this activity Operation FlashHole. Our examination reveals that the earliest evidence of this new operation dates back to July 2025. This suggests the group began preparing for the campaign shortly after ending Operation SyncHole, which lasted at least four months. We identified a minimum of three organizations impacted by the campaign in South Korea’s software, construction, and wired communication equipment manufacturing sectors. These sectors differ from those affected by Operation SyncHole, indicating that the group has expanded its target scope over time.

items.title: Valtaosa nettisivuista käyttää ohjelmointi­kieltä, josta löytyi haavoittuvuuksia
items.summary: Vakava tietoturvauhka on aiheuttanut laajoja käyttökatkoja verkkopalveluissa eri puolilla maailmaa. Suomessa verkkopalveluja on suljettu tai niiden käyttöä rajoitettu muun muassa valtionhallinnossa, yliopistoissa ja kaupungeissa. Käyttökatkoja on myös yksityisten palveluntarjoajien verkkosivuilla. Myös useissa muissa maissa verkkopalveluja on suljettu varotoimena. Tässä jutussa kerrotaan, mitä tapauksesta tiedetään. Käyttökatkojen taustalla on kaksi kriittistä tietoturva-aukkoa, jotka on löydetty laajalti käytetystä PHP-ohjelmointikielestä. PHP:tä käytetään esimerkiksi verkkosivustojen, verkkokauppojen ja muiden internetpalvelujen toiminnassa. PHP on taustalla noin 70 prosentilla verkkosivustoista, joiden ohjelmointikieli on tunnistettavissa, kertoo uutistoimisto Reuters. Tietoturvayhtiö Censysin mukaan noin 1,5 miljoonaa palvelinta käyttää sellaista PHP-versiota, johon ei ole saatavilla haavoittuvuudet korjaavaa päivitystä. Tietoturva-aukkojen aiheuttaman uhan vuoksi verkkopalveluja on varotoimena suljettu tai niiden käyttöä rajoitettu ympäri maailman.

items.title: PHP Remote Code Execution (“PHP2Shell” CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619)
items.summary: CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 are Remote Code Execution vulnerabilities in PHP, the scripting language many web servers use to run applications. It stems from stale internal data that survives after its memory is freed; a later request handled by the same worker can use that leftover data, and PHP confirms this can let an attacker run their own code on the server without logging in. Reaching the server over the network is enough; no account or prior access is needed. Unlike a typical coordinated disclosure, this one got away from everybody. On October 20, details of two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, leaked online before their coordinated disclosure and before patches were released. The PHP security team had pre-announced an emergency release for Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 14:00 UTC, but the embargo broke first: a proof-of-concept tool called “PHP2Shell” surfaced, and at least one security firm said it reproduced one of the flaws. watchTowr was the first to confirm the leak was genuine, with CEO Benjamin Harris communicating to the industry that the rumored vulnerabilities were real and that the company had successfully reproduced CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, without publishing details before the patches shipped.

items.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet
items.summary: Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them. PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others. These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it, putting every affected website in immediate risk. Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised. On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine. These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit. https://www.php2shell.com/

items.title: A tale of two PHP remote vulnerabilities
items.summary: This story outlines the details of two PHP remote vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) discovered by Calif, OpenAI and Wiz, and addressed in PHP October 2026 Security Release. To understand the bugs, first join us on a journey through time... Back then, I was a kid. I've followed Stefan's PHP research to improve my own understanding of PHP as an attack surface. Long before the 2008 call-time-pass-by-reference / interruption vulnerabilities and the more famous unserialize() use-after-frees and POP(object) injections, Stefan unearthed the first PHP memory limit remote vulnerability in 2004. I remembered the vulnerability as it was described by Stefan as being critical enough that he would not release his exploit to the public. Eventually, two other commercial exploit vendors developed non-public exploits as well - CORE and Immunity Inc. Other than those, we only had fake exploits circulating on IRC and designed to compromise your machine.
